issues.legal_issue: The restriction on oral evidence that contradicts or varies a written disposition does not apply when an insolvency representative challenges the transfer for creditors and is not acting as the insolvent’s representative in interest.
material_facts: The insolvent had executed a written deed in favour of his wife and sons, who were his representatives in interest.
After the insolvent was adjudicated, the official assignee challenged the transfer for the benefit of the creditors and sought to have it declared void.
The donees contended that, despite the deed’s description as a gift, the transaction was supported by valuable consideration and sought to lead evidence in support of that contention.
issues.conclusion: Section 92 of the Evidence Act did not apply to the proceedings, and the donees were entitled to lead evidence in support of their plea about the transaction’s true nature.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act, section 91 requires the document to prove its contents, while section 92 restricts oral evidence contradicting, varying, adding to, or subtracting from a written disposition only in disputes between parties to the instrument or their representatives in interest. Section 99 recognises the position of persons who are not parties or their representatives and does not by implication create a separate bar against oral evidence by a party or representative when the opposing side is a stranger. Under sections 17 and 55 of the Presidency-towns Insolvency Act, an official assignee challenging a transfer for the benefit of creditors does not act as the insolvent’s representative in interest; the proceeding seeks to bring transferred property back for creditors. The judgment also refers to section 53-A of the Provincial Insolvency Act, section 54-A of that Act, and the principle discussed in Phipson on Evidence with reference to R v Cheadle, 3 B. and Ad. 833.

rule.if: insolvency_transfer_challenge and assignee_acts_for_creditors and assignee_not_donor_representative and donees_are_donor_representatives

predicates.insolvency_transfer_challenge: An insolvency representative challenged a transfer made by the insolvent, seeking to have it set aside for the creditors.
predicates.assignee_acts_for_creditors: The person challenging the transfer acted for the benefit of the insolvent’s creditors.
predicates.assignee_not_donor_representative: The person challenging the transfer did not act as the transferor’s representative in interest.
predicates.donees_are_donor_representatives: The recipients of the transfer were representatives in interest of the transferor.

issues.definition: When an insolvency representative challenges a transfer for creditors without representing the transferor, and the recipients represent the transferor, oral evidence about the transaction is admissible.
